intro.title: A few practical questions.
intro.description: A starting point for deciding what to bring into scope.

items.q: Can we start with one workflow?
items.a: Yes. Start with one store or a defined workflow, then agree the tasks, workload and approvals. Additional work is reviewed before the scope changes.

items.q: Can you support several client stores?
items.a: Agency engagements can cover named stores under a shared delivery arrangement. We agree workload limits, handoffs and reporting for the portfolio.

items.q: Which platforms can you work with?
items.a: Tell us which platforms you use. We confirm relevant experience, access and delivery capacity before quoting a service or specialist project.

items.q: How do you quote the work?
items.a: A quote reflects the service, workload, complexity, coverage and review required. The scope and delivery capacity are confirmed before a proposal.

items.q: What does the free operations review include?
items.a: One workflow, using information you share, with three practical next steps in a concise one-page plan. No store login or customer records are required. Implementation is scoped separately.

hero.title: Clear ownership for everyday operations.
hero.description: Westford Operations helps e-commerce agencies and growing brands manage the work that keeps stores running, with an agreed scope, documented processes and quality checks.

intro.title: Good operations should be easy to follow.

paragraphs: A product update, a delayed order and a customer request may look like small tasks. Together they create a flow of work that needs context, ownership and follow-through. Our role is to bring that recurring work into a delivery process your team can oversee.

We agree what needs to happen, who can approve it and how progress will be reported. Work is then assigned, carried out and checked against that scope. Platform fit, delivery capacity and specialist requirements are confirmed before an engagement begins.

intro.title: A few useful details.

items.q: Do you need access to my store?
items.a: No access is needed for the initial free review. If we later agree delivery work, permissions and access are established as part of onboarding.

items.q: What if I need help across several services?
items.a: Choose the main area of support and describe the other tasks in your brief. We can discuss how those workstreams fit into a single agreed scope.
The number of stores, the type of recurring work and how your team currently hands it over are useful starting points. You can describe the situation without sharing client names or records.
